land.text: the Nellore district, where the Telugu Choda chiefs served the Imperial Cholas, Kakatiyas and Western Chalukyas ('chieftains to Imperial Cholas, Kakatiyas and Western Chalukyas', Nellore Chodas page)

predecessors.note: The Nellore Chodas were Chola feudatories: 'ruled south Andhra from 1100 to 1350 A.D.' (Telugu Cholas page); the ledger records them as a Chola vassal 1100-1208 (the whole 1100 shape lies inside Cliopatria's Chola shapes). No handover of land is recorded.

land.text: 'In 1290 CE, Rudrama's successor Prataparudra defeated Manuma-Gandagopala, whom Amba-deva had appointed to the throne of Nellore' (Ambadeva page)

successors.note: The Pandyas held Nellore from the Muttukuru campaign of 1263 (Ganapati page); the Telugu Choda line is last dated on the page by Manuma-Gandagopala's defeat in 1290. The Telugu Cholas page lists the Nellore line to 1350 without dated land.

capitals.name: Vikramasimhapuri (Nellore)
capitals.note: 'Vikramasimhapuri (modern Nellore)' is the capital on the Nellore Chodas page; the Kanchi seat of Vijaya Gandagopala (Ganapati page) is not treated as a capital. The span ends in 1262 because the dossier holds no land from the 1263 loss of Nellore (ledger) to the 1281 restoration; the Pandya and Kakatiya reading of 1263-1280 is in the notes.

capitals.name: Vikramasimhapuri (Nellore)
capitals.note: Nellore again from the restoration of Manuma Ganda-gopala, 'on the throne of Nellore' (Ambadeva page), to Prataparudra's victory in 1290. Capital span split after review.

correction.text: 'They ruled over their kingdom consisting of the Nellore, Cuddapah, Chittoor and Chengalput districts' (Nellore Chodas page): Nellore, Tirupati (for Chittoor), Kanchipuram (for Chengalpattu) and a coordinate at Kadapa (Cuddapah) approximate the four districts

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria shape exists). The page names four districts and no boundary; the infobox gives no area, so no comparison with a Cliopatria shape is possible. The same page says Tikka (1223-1248) 'extended his kingdom to as far south as the river Kaveri' without a place or year; that extension is not drawn. The Kakatiya dossier draws Nellore as a Kakatiya vassal 1208-1263 over this same land. Review fix: the whole shape lies inside Cliopatria's Chola Empire shapes (about 41,981 km2 in 1100, 38,947 in 1160, 31,107 in 1200-1249), so the ledger now records the Chola vassalage 1100-1208 and the Kakatiya vassalage 1208-1263. Nellore Chodas page reread: Tikka (1223-1248) 'extended his kingdom to as far south as the river Kaveri' and 'got thereby the Tondaimandalam region for himself' after defeating 'both the Hoyasala and the Pandyan forces'; no year within 1223-1248, no places, so only Tondaimandalam (already inside the Kanchipuram/Chengalpattu circle) is covered and the Kaveri extension stays undrawn.

minus.text: 'They ruled over their kingdom consisting of the Nellore, Cuddapah, Chittoor and Chengalput districts' (Nellore Chodas page): Nellore, Tirupati (for Chittoor), Kanchipuram (for Chengalpattu) and a coordinate at Kadapa (Cuddapah) approximate the four districts

correction.text: the four districts without Kanchipuram, which 'Pandyan forces ... captured ... in 1258' (Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan I page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the kingdom after the Pandyas took Kanchipuram. The pages do not say what else Vijaya Gandagopala kept; the 1260 overrun of his territory (Nellore Chodas page) and the 1257 invasion belong to the contest below.

correction.text: Nellore, where Manuma Ganda-gopala sat on the throne with Ambadeva's backing, 'sometime before 1282'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: only the Nellore throne is attested after 1263. Between 1263 and 1281 the dossier holds no land: pandya-empire draws Nellore as Pandya (ledger 11) until it passes to the Kakatiyas by 1271 (ledger 15; Naga-deva 1271-1275, kakatiya-dynasty ledgers 13 and 16). The Ganapati page says the Choda brothers ruled Nellore 'as Pandya vassals' and the Ambadeva page implies that Vijaya Ganda-gopala held it until 1279; neither gives years, so they are not drawn.

region.text: 'They ruled over their kingdom consisting of the Nellore, Cuddapah, Chittoor and Chengalput districts' (Nellore Chodas page): Nellore, Tirupati (for Chittoor), Kanchipuram (for Chengalpattu) and a coordinate at Kadapa (Cuddapah) approximate the four districts

ledger.note: c. 1100: the Nellore Chodas appear as the south Andhra branch. 'nellore Chodas was the most predominant Chola branch who ruled south Andhra from 1100 to 1350 A.D.' The page gives the span, not a founding act; the land is the Nellore Chodas page's four districts with Vikramasimhapuri (Nellore) as capital.

region.text: the Nellore Chodas' four districts under the Cholas: 'chieftains to Imperial Cholas, Kakatiyas and Western Chalukyas'; 'owed nominal allegiance to the already crippled Later Cholas' (Nellore Chodas page)

ledger.note: c. 1100 (rounded start, as the found event): the Nellore Choda chiefs are Chola feudatories. Nellore Chodas page: they were 'chieftains to Imperial Cholas'; Ganapati page: 'Nalla-siddhi and his younger brother Tammu-siddhi ruled as Chola vassals till 1207-1208' and the Nellore Choda chiefs 'were Chola vassals'. The whole of the 1100 shape lies inside Cliopatria's Chola Empire shapes (about 41,981 km2 in 1100, 38,947 in 1160, 31,107 in 1200-1249 on the grid), so the state is drawn as the Chola vassal until the Kakatiya installation. Added after review: the chola-empire dossier carries no mirror pair yet.

region.text: the same four districts; the Chola vassalage ends where the Ganapati page's Chola-vassal span ends: 'ruled as Chola vassals till 1207-1208'

ledger.note: 1208: the Chola hold on Nellore ends. Ganapati page: Nalla-siddhi and Tammu-siddhi 'ruled as Chola vassals till 1207-1208'; then Ganapati 'marched to Nellore, forced Tammu-siddhi to flee, and installed Tikka'. The page adds that Tikka 'later also appeased Kulottunga III by acknowledging his suzerainty' with no year (not drawn), and the Nellore Chodas page has Tikka owing 'nominal allegiance to the already crippled Later Cholas'. chola-empire ledger 34 (c. 1177, the Chola north shrinks) is the other possible end; the page-dated 1207-1208 is used.

region.text: the Choda kingdom under Tikka: Ganapati 'installed Tikka on the throne as Tikka-bhupala'

ledger.note: 1208 (bridge): Ganapati installs Tikka at Nellore. 'Ganapati marched to Nellore, forced Tammu-siddhi to flee, and installed Tikka on the throne as Tikka-bhupala.' The page gives no year for it; it follows 'ruled as Chola vassals till 1207-1208' and the page places Ganapati's southern campaign before the 1213 Chebrolu inscription. Mirror of kakatiya-dynasty ledger 5, which uses the same bridge. Added after review.

region.text: Nellore, the kingdom of Manuma-siddhi II and Vijaya Gandagopala

ledger.note: c. 1257: the Pandyas invade Nellore. 'Manumasiddhi, also known as Vira-gandagopala, the Telugu Chola ruler of Nellore ... faced renewed pressure from the south following the invasion of Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I around c. 1257 CE.' The Ganapati page agrees ('around 1257'); the Nellore Chodas page says 1260.

1258: the Pandyas take Kanchipuram and kill Vijaya Gandagopala. 'Pandyan forces killed the Telugu Choda ruler Vijaya Gandagopala of Nellore Chodas and captured Kanchipuram in 1258.' The pandya-empire dossier records the gain (ledger 10).

region.text: the Choda kingdom whose ruler Manuma-siddhi II was killed at Muttukuru

ledger.note: 1263: the Kakatiya vassalage ends with the Pandya conquest. 'In 1248, Ganapati's Nellore Choda vassal Tikka died' (his son Manuma-siddhi II succeeded); 'The Pandyas captured Nellore, and killed Manuma-siddhi II in the Battle of Muttukuru in 1263 CE.' Mirror of kakatiya-dynasty ledger 11. Added after review.
1263: the fighting for Nellore ends at Muttukuru. 'The Pandyas captured Nellore, and killed Manuma-siddhi II in the Battle of Muttukuru in 1263 CE.'

region.text: Nellore and the rest of the Choda kingdom (Chittoor and Cuddapah districts), which the page does not name separately

ledger.note: 1263: Nellore passes to the Pandyas. 'The Pandyas captured Nellore'; 'The brothers of Manuma-siddhi II accepted the Pandya suzerainty, agreeing to rule Nellore as Pandya vassals.' The Jatavarman page says 'Sundara Pandyan annexed Kanchi, Nellore and Visayavadai' without a year, and pandya-empire dates its Nellore gain 1258; the Ganapati page's 1263 is the only dated capture of Nellore. The page names Nellore; Chittoor and Cuddapah are the researcher's reading of the Nellore Chodas page's four districts.

before 1281: Manuma Ganda-gopala regains the Nellore throne. 'Sometime before 1281, Amba-deva appointed Manuma Ganda-gopala on the throne of' Nellore (Rudrama Devi page); the Ambadeva page says 'sometime before 1282' and has Manuma seek Amba-deva's help 'After Vijaya's death in 1279'. Counterpart corrected after review from pandya-empire to kakatiya-dynasty: pandya-empire ledger 15 loses Nellore to the Kakatiyas by 1271 (Naga-deva, 'a vassal of Rudrama, ruled at Nellore during 1271-1275', Rudrama Devi page) and kakatiya-dynasty ledgers 13 and 16 hold it. The same page has a Telugu Choda, Tiru-kalatti-deva II, ruling Nellore 'c. 1279-1283, before another Choda chief Manuma-Gandagopala displaced him'; the pages do not agree on who sat at Nellore 1279-1281, so the year stays at the 'before 1281' bridge. kakatiya-dynasty needs the matching c. 1281 loss.

region.text: Nellore, where Amba-deva 'appointed Manuma Ganda-gopala on the throne'

ledger.note: before 1281/1282: Manuma Ganda-gopala holds Nellore as Ambadeva's nominee. 'After Vijaya's death in 1279, Manuma sought Amba-deva's help to regain control of Nellore'; Amba-deva's appointment 'must have taken place sometime before 1282' (Ambadeva page; the Rudrama Devi page says 'Sometime before 1281'). 1281 is the year of kayastha-principality-of-ambadeva ledger 2. Added after review.

region.text: Nellore, the throne to which Amba-deva had appointed Manuma-Gandagopala

ledger.note: 1290: Ambadeva's hold on Nellore ends when 'Rudrama's successor Prataparudra defeated Manuma-Gandagopala, whom Amba-deva had appointed to the throne of Nellore.' Mirror of kayastha-principality-of-ambadeva ledger 3. Added after review.

region.text: Nellore, the throne to which Amba-deva had appointed Manuma-Gandagopala

ledger.note: 1290: the Kakatiyas take Nellore. 'In 1290 CE, Rudrama's successor Prataparudra defeated Manuma-Gandagopala, whom Amba-deva had appointed to the throne of Nellore.' The Nellore Chodas page says only that under Prataparudra II 'the Nellore region became part and parcel of the Kakatiya empire'.

1290: the Telugu Chodas of Nellore end with Manuma-Gandagopala's defeat. The Telugu Cholas page lists later Nellore chiefs (Rajagandagopala, Viragandagopala) and a span 'to 1350' but dates no land to them, so 1290 is the last dated act of the line.

wars.name: Pandya invasion of Nellore
wars.outcome: Pandya victory: Kanchipuram captured in 1258, Nellore in 1263 at Muttukuru, where Manuma-siddhi II was killed; his brothers ruled as Pandya vassals.
wars.note: The pages disagree on dates: 1257 invasion (Jatavarman page), 1258 death of Vijaya Gandagopala, 1260 overrun (Nellore Chodas page), 1263 Muttukuru (Ganapati page). A Kakatiya army was beaten 'at Mudugur in the current Nellore district' (undated).

wars.name: Kakatiya campaign against Manuma-Gandagopala
wars.outcome: Kakatiya victory: Prataparudra defeats the Nellore ruler appointed by Amba-deva in 1290 and Nellore becomes Kakatiya land.
wars.note: Amba-deva himself was defeated in 1291 ('between 13 June and 11 August 1291'), outside this state's life.

certainty.note: The pages name districts and cities, never a boundary; the Pandya-Kakatiya frontier around Nellore moved with each campaign (1257-1263, 1279-1290).

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (no row). Dates are shaky: the Telugu Cholas page gives only the span 1100-1350 for the Nellore line and the Nellore Chodas page dates only Tikka (1223-1248) and Vijaya Gandagopala (1248-1263), so the 1100 start is a rounded figure from that span (confidence 2) and the 1290 end is the last dated act (Manuma-Gandagopala's defeat). The pages disagree on the Pandya conquest (1257, 1258, 1260, 1263) and on Vijaya Gandagopala, killed in 1258 on the Jatavarman page, reigning to 1263 on the Nellore Chodas page and ruling Kanchi, with inscriptions, 'until 1282' on the Ganapati page (the Ambadeva page has him dying in 1279); the dossier records every date as a page gives it. Vassal relations are not recorded here because the overlord records them: kakatiya-dynasty ledger 5 and 11 (Kakatiya vassal 1208-1263; Tikka installed, page silent on year; Ganapati page: Nalla-siddhi and Tammu-siddhi 'ruled as Chola vassals till 1207-1208', and about 1180 Kulottunga III installed Nalla-siddhi in place of Manuma-siddhi I), kayastha-principality-of-ambadeva ledger 2 and 3. The existing dossiers do not agree with each other on 1258 vs 1263 for the Pandya hold on Nellore; the contest 1257-1263 covers both. The pandya-empire dossier has no matching vassal or loss for 1279-1281, so the 1281 gain (confidence 1) has no counterpart event. Natural Earth has no Kadapa, Chittoor or Chengalpattu place, so the four districts are drawn from Nellore, Tirupati, Kanchipuram and a coordinate at Kadapa (78.82E 14.47N); the gazetteer agent could add Kadapa (Cuddapah), Chittoor and Chengalpattu. The Wikipedia title of the state's article is not confirmed: the tool returned no title for Nellore_Chodas. REVIEW FIXES (2026-11-01): added the Chola vassal pair 1100-1208 and the Kakatiya pair 1208-1263 and the Ambadeva pair 1281-1290 (mirrors of kakatiya-dynasty ledger 5 and 11 and kayastha-principality-of-ambadeva ledger 2 and 3; chola-empire has no mirror yet); the 1281 gain now has kakatiya-dynasty as counterpart; the Nellore capital is split around the 1263-1280 gap. Open: the Ganapati page's 'Pandya vassals' and the Ambadeva page's implication that Vijaya Ganda-gopala held Nellore to 1279 would put Choda rule on Nellore inside 1263-1280; the pages give no years, so the span stays empty.
